extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying commutative algebra (primary decomposition, radicals, integral dependence, localization, valuation rings)
extracted.subtask_description: Supplementary textbook/lecture-note statements and lemmas about primary decomposition of modules/submodules, properties of the module-radical r_M(·), behavior under localization and quotients, and basic results on integral extensions and valuation rings. Contains claims, propositions, and proofs used to fill missing steps in a commutative algebra text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXVII (primary ideal annihilator property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Q be a P-primary ideal. If IJ ⊆ Q and I ⊄ Q then J ⊆ P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: pick x ∈ I  ackslash Q; for any y ∈ J, xy ∈ Q ⊆ P. Since x ∉ Q and Q is primary, some power of y lies in Q, hence y ∈ P because r(Q)=P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.3 (intersection of p-primary submodules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Qi is p-primary for i = 1,2,···,n submodules of M, then Q = ⋂_{i=1}^n Qi is also p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: Show any zero divisor on M/Q is nilpotent by using that it is nilpotent on each M/Qi; take a common exponent n to see x^n M ⊆ Q. For the radical, r(Q:M)=⋂ r(Qi:M)=p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.4 (colons with primary submodule)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If x ∈ Q then (Q:x) = (1). (b) If x ∉ Q then (Q:x) is p-primary and hence r(Q:x)=p. (c) If x ∉ p then (Q:x) = Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketches: (a) trivial. For (b) show if yz ∈ (Q:x) but y ∉ (Q:x) then z is a zero-divisor on M/Q so nilpotent hence z^n ∈ (Q:x). Then deduce p ⊆ r(Q:x) and conversely elements of r(Q:x) map to p by applying nilpotence argument. For (c) use nilpotence contradiction to prove (Q:x)⊆Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.5 (primes from minimal primary decomposition are r(N:m))
rubrics_metrics.description: If N = ⋂_{i=1}^n Qi is a minimal primary decomposition with pi = r_M(Qi), then the pi are precisely the prime ideals which occur in the set { r(N:m) | m ∈ M }, hence are independent of the particular decomposition of N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: For fixed i choose m ∈ ⋂_{j≠i} Qj  ackslash Qi; then (N:m) = (Qi:m) is pi-primary, so each pi = r(N:m). Conversely any r(N:m) prime equals some pi by factoring (N:m)=⋂ (Qi:m) and Exercise 1.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotients preserve primaryness and radicals (statement 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a decomposable submodule N with minimal primary decomposition N = ⋂_{i=1}^n Qi, the quotient Qi/N is r_{M/N}(Qi/N)-primary with r_{M/N}(Qi/N) = r_M(Qi). Conversely, Qi/N primary implies Qi primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use (Qi/N : M/N) = (Qi : M) to identify radicals; primaryness follows since (M/N)/(Qi/N) ≅ M/Qi and zero-divisors/nilpotence transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.6 (minimal primes belong to N / containment property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N be decomposable. Any prime p ⊇ r_M(N) contains a minimal prime ideal belonging to N. Hence the minimal prime ideals of N are precisely the minimal elements among prime ideals containing N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minimal primary decomposition N = ⋂ Qi and r_M(N)=⋂ r_M(Qi); any p containing this intersection must contain some r_M(Qj) and hence contains the corresponding minimal prime belonging to N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.7 (radical of decomposable N and zero-divisors union)
rubrics_metrics.description: If N = ⋂_{i=1}^n Qi is a minimal primary decomposition and r_M(Qi) = pi, then r_M(N) = ⋂_{i=1}^n pi. In particular, when N=0 decomposable the set D of zero-divisors of M is the union of the prime ideals belonging to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument reduces to N=0. Show D = { x ∈ A : (0:x) ≠ 0 } and r(D)=D, then express D as union/intersection of r(0:m), and use Exercise 1.11/Exercise 4.22 uniqueness to finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of r_M(N) (items (a)–(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collected properties of the module radical r_M(N): (a) If N ⊆ P ⊆ M then r_M(N) ⊆ r_M(P). (b) For algebras C ⊆ B over A, r_B(C^n) = r_B(C) for any n. (c) For f:A→B, r_B(f^{-1}(b)) ⊇ f^{-1}(b) for any ideal b of B. (d) r(r_M(N)) = r_M(N). (e) r_M(N ∩ P) = r_M(N) ∩ r_M(P). (f) r_M(N) = (1) ⇔ M = N. (g) r_M(N+P) ⊇ r(r_M(N)+r_M(P)) (converse false).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each property has short direct proofs: monotonicity, radical idempotence, behaviour under algebra maps, radicals of intersections and sums, and counterexample for (g) converse is given (M=A⊕A with N=A⊕0, P=0⊕A).

rubrics_metrics.name: (Q:M) is primary (Exercise 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Q primary submodule of M, the annihilator (Q:M) = Ann(M/Q) is primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If xy∈(Q:M) but y∉(Q:M), consider multiplication endomorphisms on M/Q and deduce x is a zero-divisor hence nilpotent; so some power of x lies in (Q:M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.8 (localization of primary modules)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If S∩p ≠ ∅ then S^{-1}Q = S^{-1}M. (b) If S∩p = ∅ then S^{-1}Q is S^{-1}p-primary and its contraction in M is Q. Thus primary modules in S^{-1}M correspond to primary modules of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: (a) if s∈S∩p then s^n M⊆Q so every element of S^{-1}M is in S^{-1}Q. (b) Zero-divisors/nilpotence arguments show S^{-1}Q is primary and r_{S^{-1}M}(S^{-1}Q)=S^{-1}p; contraction and extension arguments show correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.9 (localization of minimal primary decomposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N decomposable with minimal primary decomposition N=⋂_{i=1}^n Qi and pi = r_M(Qi). Number so that S meets p_{m+1},...,p_n but not p_1,...,p_m. Then S^{-1}N = ⋂_{i=1}^m S^{-1}Qi and S(N) = ⋂_{i=1}^m Qi; these are minimal primary decompositions in S^{-1}M and in M respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 4.8 and contraction/extension arguments; show minimality and distinctness of S^{-1}pi; contraction gives uniqueness contradiction if not minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.10 & Corollary 4.11 (isolated primary components uniqueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For N decomposable with minimal primary decomposition N=⋂ Qi and an isolated set {pi1,...,pim} of prime ideals of N, the corresponding intersection of Qi over those isolated primes gives a primary decomposition of S(N) and the isolated primary components (those corresponding to minimal prime ideals) are uniquely determined by N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take S = A  igcup_{k} p_k (complement of union of other pis); apply Proposition 4.9 to get S(N) and show independence of choice by the multiplicative set S. Corollary: isolated (minimal) components are uniquely determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXVIII (finite iff finite type + integral)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring homomorphism f:A→B is finite if and only if it is of finite type and integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finite type and integral, B=A[b1,...,bn] and Corollary 5.2 implies B is a finitely generated A-module. Conversely, if B is a finitely generated A-module then it is finite type and each generator is integral over A, so B is integral over A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXIX (finitely generated domain that is a field is algebraic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be an integral domain finitely generated as a k-algebra. If A is a field, then A is algebraic over the base field k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on number of generators: if one generator is transcendental contradiction, reduce by adjoining generators and use that fields finitely generated over a field must be algebraic extension when they are fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXX (valuation ring extension via Zorn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A ⊆ K a subring of field K and a homomorphism f:A→Ω (Ω some field), there exists a valuation ring B with A ⊆ B ⊆ K and an extension g:B→Ω of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the set Σ of pairs (C,h) with A⊆C⊆K and h|A=f, order by inclusion, take maximal element via Zorn; maximal element yields valuation ring by Theorem 5.21; g extends f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.21 (maximal element yields valuation ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (B,g) is a maximal element of the poset Σ of extensions, then B is a valuation ring of the field K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: maximality forces units/outside maximal ideal behaviour; uses maximality and arguments that any larger ring or ideal would contradict maximality, concluding valuation property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 5.19 (locality of B in maximal pair)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (B,g) is maximal in Σ then B is a local ring and m = ker(g) is its maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show B = B_m so elements outside m are units (1/s ∈ B for s ∈ A ackslash m) and apply standard result that this makes B local.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral extensions induce closed maps on Spec (1.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B is integral (and factor through f(A)⊆B), then the induced map f^*: Spec(B)→Spec(A) is closed; equivalently s^*: Spec(B)→Spec(f(A)) is closed when f(A) is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove s^*(V(b)) = V(b ∩ f(A)) using Proposition 5.6 and Theorem 5.10 applied to B/b and f(A)/(b∩f(A)), then lift primes to get surjectivity and closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of homomorphisms to integral extensions (2.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f:A→Ω with ker(f)=m maximal, and B integral over A, there exists an extension g:B→Ω (constructed by passing to quotient B/𝔪' integral over A/m and using Zorn-type maximal extension argument to embed C[...]/(minimal polynomial) into Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to integral domains and extend maps by adjoining integral elements and using algebraically closed Ω to realize root-adjoining maps; use Zorn's lemma/inductive extension to reach B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product preserves integrality (3.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is integral over A then for any A-algebra C the tensor product B ⊗_A C is integral over (f⊗1)(B) (or over B ⊗_A C's image of B). Equivalently, basic tensors b⊗c are integral over the image of f⊗1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a monic relation for b over A then tensor with C and observe the coefficients lie in the image so the tensor is integral; extend to finite sums of tensors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample: localization of integral extension need not be integral (4.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: char k = 2, B = k[x], A = k[x^2−1]; B is integral over A but localization B_n (at n=(x−1)) is not integral over A_m where m = n∩A = (x^2−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through alleged integral relation for 1/(x+1) in localized ring to derive contradictions using multiplicatively closed sets and divisor properties; shows integrality need not localize in this naive sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXI (maximal ideals correspondence under integral extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊆ B and B integral over A, then maximal ideals correspond bijectively by extension and contraction: max(B) ↔ max(A). Consequently the Jacobson radicals satisfy Rad(A) = A ∩ Rad(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 5.10 and Corollary 5.8 to lift/contract primes and show maxima correspond; then compute Jacobson radical as intersection over maximal ideals and compare via contraction/extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXII (adjoin roots to split monic polynomial)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any monic polynomial f∈B[x] there exists an extension ring D⊇B in which f splits as a product of linear monic factors (i.e., one can adjoin roots successively: D_1=B[x]/(f), then factor out linear factor and iterate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on deg(f): form D1=B[x]/(f) where x is a root, factor f=(t−x)f1 in D1[t], reduce degree and iterate to split over a larger ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXIV (homeomorphism for purely inseparable finite extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A integrally closed domain with fraction field K and L a finite purely inseparable extension of K; let B be integral closure of A in L. Then the induced map f^*: Spec(B)→Spec(A) is a homeomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show f^* is bijective (explicit construction of preimage ideals via p-power membership) and continuous; apply that integral maps are closed to conclude homeomorphism; hence every fiber is singleton.
